# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b61 - Select an external power switch in any state

Beta61 extends Beta60. It preserves the canonical `environment_manager` domain, stored `switch.*` IDs, friendly labels, all room/device settings, PID behavior, and physical safety constraints.

## Fix: selecting a supply is not taking control of its power

- Pair a dedicated, same-room external power switch when Home Assistant reports it **ON**, **OFF**, **unavailable**, **unknown**, or has no live state yet. A running appliance may also be selected. The dropdown stores the physical switch's immutable identity; no switch service call is issued by the selection.
- A previously ON supply is **not automatically adopted** or turned OFF by the controller. The native appliance may continue its normal independently authorized control. An unavailable supply waits for genuine state data rather than being assumed OFF.
- An unowned supply can be deselected while ON or unavailable. Changing a previously controller-owned or pending supply still requires safe reconciliation.
- The `switch.*` registry identity, same-area restriction, generated-controller/self-output exclusions and cross-controller claim checks are retained, including a second identity/claim check immediately before config persistence. Live switch state changes while editing never invalidate a harmless selection.

## Prevent accidental power control after pairing

- Physical supply OFF is never inferred from the downstream appliance going unavailable. Unavailable native outputs do not count as verified idle.
- While a separately controlled native output still has a controller-owned ON cycle or pending command, an OFF supply is held; no external power ON is issued. A second dispatch-time guard enforces this even if the device's state changes between scheduling and service execution.
- Actual external supply **ON** requires genuine previously verified native capabilities, fresh actionable demand, occupancy/window policies, startup warmup, minimum physical OFF duration, matching physical identity, and service acknowledgment. If no capability model has ever been verified, automatic ON waits without inventing one.
- External supply **OFF** remains restricted to supply power actually owned by the manager after a confirmed prior ON command, proven idle native outputs and the configured cooldown. An already-ON switch selected by the user is never treated as owned solely due to its ON state.
- Native relay ownership after a manual switch OFF remains subject to existing manual override and reconciliation logic; selection neither claims nor reverses manual power changes.

## Validation

CI executes actual `EquipmentRuntime.async_update`, `before_tick`, and `_dispatch_safe` code under isolated Home Assistant registry/state stubs. Scenarios include both native capability paths, the ON/OFF/unavailable/unknown/missing switch-state matrix, available/running/disconnected native devices, selection races, rejection of claimed identities, reconfiguration of controller-owned supplies, changes to a running native controller, idle-native ownership holds, and zero switch service calls during selection. The release publisher verifies Python and JavaScript syntax, all JSON catalogs, canonical ZIP packaging and the `environment_manager` domain.

Live Home Assistant and appliance behavior still needs confirmation on actual hardware.

## Installation

In HACS, open the **existing** Home Environment Manager integration, show beta versions, select **v0.6.0b61**, install and restart Home Assistant. Do not add a second integration. The manual ZIP contains `custom_components/environment_manager/`.
